title: Statistics - Lesson 4: Outliers Practice
description: Practice identifying possible outliers with the 1.5 x IQR rule and explaining their effect.

questions.question: What is the interquartile range, or IQR?
questions.explanation: The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of the data and is found by subtracting Q1 from Q3.

questions.question: Which formula gives the upper fence?
questions.explanation: The upper fence is Q3 plus 1.5 times the IQR. Values above this fence are possible high outliers.

questions.question: If Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 20, what is the IQR? Enter just the number.
If Q1 = 10, Q3 = 18, and IQR = 8, what is the upper fence? Enter just the number.
For the data 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 30, the upper fence is 16. Which value is a possible outlier?
questions.explanation: Since 30 is greater than the upper fence of 16, it is a possible high outlier.

questions.question: A value flagged as a possible outlier should always be deleted from the data set.
questions.explanation: A possible outlier should be investigated first. It might be an error, a special case, or an important real value.

questions.question: Which statistic is usually more resistant to one extremely high value?
questions.explanation: The median depends on position, so one extreme high value usually changes it less than it changes the mean.

questions.question: A data set has one possible high outlier. In one or two sentences, explain how that outlier could affect a conclusion about a typical value.
questions.correctAnswer: A high outlier can pull the mean upward, making the typical value seem larger than most data values. The median or the main cluster may better describe the typical value.
questions.explanation: A strong answer mentions that a high outlier can raise the mean and that the median or cluster may better describe a typical value.
